title: Austin Paves Streets, Adjusts Taxes, & Early Auto Perks
summary:
*   **Massive Street Improvement Projects:** The city initiated extensive grading, paving, and guttering for numerous streets, including West 19th, 9th, 6th, Colorado, Guadalupe, and Brazos. Property owners were assessed costs, and legal action was directed against those who refused to agree to payment.
*   **Widespread Tax Assessment Corrections:** Multiple residents received adjustments or outright cancellations for their 1912-1913 tax assessments, primarily concerning "money on hand" or "credits," often due to documented errors.
*   **Glimpses into Early Automobile Life:** The Council remitted a speeding fine for an automobile driver and granted a permit for a "Quick Service Fire Repair Company" to install a "free air" pipe for cars under a sidewalk.
*   **Unique Public & Private Matters:** The city issued duplicate cemetery deeds, authorized payment for a lost employee warrant, and notably, credited the Austin Statesman newspaper for employee wages lost during a severe storm that caused a city power outage.

The Mayor laid the following resolution before the Council:--- Whereas, it appears that
the deed executed by John McDonald, Mayor of the City of Austin, Texas, on the 12th day of
June, 1890, to Christian Kofahl, of the Northeast Quarter of Cemetery Lot No. 720, in the
Austin City Cemetery, was not acknowledged, and therefore could not be placed of record.
Now therefore, BE IT RESOLVED, by the City Council of the City of Austin, that A. P.
Wooldridge, Mayor, be and he is hereby authorized to execute a duplicate deed to Christian
Kofahl, his heirs and assigns, in lieu of the original deed heretofore executed by the
said John McDonald, Mayor, on the said 12th day of June, 1890, and to attach to said
duplicate deed, said original deed of John McDonald to Christian Kofahl and make it a part
of said duplicate deed.
